newsitem.title: CAMBODIA: Cambodia appeals for aid for impoverished schools.
newsitem.headline: Cambodia appeals for aid for impoverished schools.

text.p: Cambodia on Thursday appealed for aid for its overburdened and corrupt school system, saying it needs $60 million by the end of the century.
Education Minister Tol Lah told a news conference it would ask the "international community and other governments" for help.
"Some schools are very old and need repairs, and we need to build new ones," he said.
Tol Lah predicted the number of students would swell from two million to three million by the end of the century in a country that only has between 7,000 and 8,000 classrooms.
Cambodia recently borrowed $20 million from the Asian Development Bank for teaching programmes, he said.
Cambodia's educational system is plagued by a lack of qualified teachers, few books, strained budgets and corruption, analysts say.
Teachers were paid less than $30 per month, Tol Lah said.
"We want to increase this, but we have no money, so this is a big problem of the ministry," he said.
The average child in Cambodia completes less than four years in school, and only one third of children over the age of seven attend any kind of educational institution.
